purpose: Demonstrate that W7900 compute can produce an MTP speedup under a native C++ orchestration path; this is design evidence for a cross-backend native speculative cycle launcher, not a promoted hipEngine result.

protocol.timing: llama.cpp predicted_ms starts after the first sampled output; transition rates use (predicted_n - 1 per request) / predicted_ms

comparison_context.interpretation: llama.cpp MTP is faster despite slightly lower accepted/output, so W7900 compute and acceptance are not the primary blockers; hipEngine launch/orchestration cost is the main portability gap.

command: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python3 scripts/llamacpp_mtp_bench.py --server-bin /home/lhl/llama.cpp/llama.cpp-hip/build-gfx1100-therock715/bin/llama-server --model /models/gguf/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_M.gguf --ctx-size 8192 --concurrency 1 --gpu-layers 99 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --draft-max 2 --mode both --protocol natural --prompts benchmarks/prompts/mtpbench-code-general-ja.jsonl --max-tokens 25 --seed 12345 --temperature 0 --top-k 1 --top-p 1 --min-p 0 --server-extra-arg=--reasoning --server-extra-arg=off --output /tmp/w7900-llamacpp-gfx1100-base-mtp-natural25-current.json
notes: External diagnostic only: llama.cpp uses F16 KV and a preserved dirty instrumentation patchset, while hipEngine uses BF16 KV.
The transition speedup ratio is unaffected by the untimed-first-output numerator correction because base and MTP use the same request count and output horizon.
No hipEngine performance row is promoted by this artifact.
